Limousine bus：Airport limousine buses run from Incheon Airport toward Myeongdong; you walk from the stop to your hotel. The fare is around KRW 17,000.
Taxi：Board at the taxi stand right outside the arrivals hall. Expect about KRW 58,000–72,000 (estimated from November 2026 fares, excluding late-night surcharge).

Transfer：No transfers from the arrivals hall exit to your hotel entrance. The fare is a fixed KRW 150,000 (for 1 vehicle). Central Myeongdong is a maze of busy pedestrian lanes, and cars cannot enter at certain times. At some hotels you get in and out on the main road.
Which option should you choose?
Late arrival：Street food stalls stay open into the evening, but the streets empty out late at night. With a transfer, you don't have to worry about the taxi late-night surcharge (20–40%).
Group travel：A Staria fits 6 passengers plus 4–5 large suitcases. With 4 people, 1 person pays KRW 37,500.

First visit：Myeongdong's big plus is that street food alleys and cosmetics shops are right outside your hotel after check-in. Stalls set up from early evening. Skip the tiring transit and start sightseeing on arrival day.
Solo traveler：Take the AREX airport railroad to Seoul Station, then switch to Subway Line 4; Myeongdong Station is 2 stops away. The train is the cheapest option.

Incheon Airport's taxi stands are right outside the arrivals hall, with separate stands for regular, deluxe (mobeom) and jumbo taxis. Deluxe (mobeom) taxis cost more than regular ones, but some of their drivers speak Japanese or English.

With a transfer, the driver waits at the arrivals exit, carries your luggage and walks you to the car. Walkerhill sits on a hilltop, and walking from the nearest station isn't realistic. Going directly from the airport to the hotel's drop-off area is by far the easiest.
Recommendations by situation

Late or early：There is little transport out of the hotels at night, so a taxi or chartered car is handy if you plan to go out. With a transfer, we wait for your flight, and the fare is the same as during the day.
Group travel：A Staria fits 6 passengers plus 4–5 large suitcases. With 4 people, 1 person pays KRW 37,500.
First visit：These hotels overlook the Han River and suit a relaxed stay enjoying the in-house restaurants and shows. Skip the tiring transit and start sightseeing on arrival day.
Solo traveler：By train there are several transfers, and you need to catch the hotel shuttle bus from Gwangnaru Station on Subway Line 5. The train is the cheapest option.

From Incheon Airport, the route crosses Yeongjong Bridge or Incheon Bridge and enters Seoul on the Incheon International Airport Expressway. To reach Walkerhill it usually continues along Gangbyeonbuk-ro (north bank of the Han River), detouring onto city streets when the riverside road is congested.

A hilltop hotel complex overlooking the Han River (Grand Walkerhill and Vista Walkerhill), away from the nearest station. Main hotels are Grand Walkerhill Seoul and Vista Walkerhill Seoul. Just tell us your hotel name and we will drop you at its entrance at Walkerhill.

icn-songdo-ikikata.h1: Incheon Airport to Songdo: Train, Bus, Taxi and Transfer Compared
icn-songdo-ikikata.lead: Songdo is Incheon's new city, home to Central Park, high-rise hotels and G-Tower, in a different direction from Seoul. We compare the train, bus and car options from Incheon Airport to Songdo by fare and number of transfers.
secs: 4 ways to get from Incheon Airport to Songdo
By train：2 transfers. Songdo is just across Incheon Bridge from the airport, in the opposite direction from Seoul. The train involves several transfers, so a bus or car is more convenient.
Limousine bus：Airport limousine buses run from Incheon Airport toward Songdo; you walk from the stop to your hotel. The fare is around KRW 17,000.
Taxi：Board at the taxi stand right outside the arrivals hall. Expect about KRW 35,000–42,000 (estimated from November 2026 fares, excluding late-night surcharge).

Transfer：No transfers from the arrivals hall exit to your hotel entrance. The fare is quoted on request. Songdo's roads are wide with little congestion, so travel time from the airport is easy to predict.
Which option should you choose?
Late or early：The streets are fairly quiet at night, and shops don't stay open as late as in Seoul. With a transfer, we wait for your flight, and there is no surcharge for the time of day.
2+ with luggage：The train means 2 transfers, which is no fun with suitcases.
Kids or seniors：We can provide child seats free of charge. No transfers all the way to your Songdo hotel entrance.
Solo traveler：Songdo is just across Incheon Bridge from the airport, in the opposite direction from Seoul. The train is the cheapest option.
